notes:
A gift upgrade can now only raise what a member can use, never lower it. If you granted someone the Studio features while they paid for Solo, and they later moved themselves up to Agency, the old gift stayed in place and quietly held them at Studio - paying for the top plan while using the middle one, with nothing on screen to say so. The gift is now compared against the plan they pay for and only applies when it is the stronger of the two.

The "a new version is available" box appears even on a slow connection. The check at startup gives up after six seconds so it never holds up the app; if the answer arrived after that, the box was never shown for the rest of that session. The check now opens the box itself when it finishes late.

You can now give a paying member the features of a higher plan as a gift, without changing what they are charged. If a friend buys Solo, you can grant them the Agency features and Stripe keeps billing them Solo every month, exactly as before. Until now this was impossible and trying it broke three things at once: the plan you set by hand was quietly written back by the payment provider at the next renewal, so the member lost the features a month later; the revenue figure broke, because setting a plan by hand marks the row as granted, and answering "gift" made a member who really pays disappear from the monthly total; and the money never changed anyway, since nothing here talks to the payment provider. The gift is now a separate field. The plan they pay for is untouched, so revenue still counts what they actually pay, and the gift is not something the payment provider writes, so renewals leave it alone. It applies only while the subscription is active - if they cancel, the gift falls away with it - and a mistyped plan name is refused rather than silently dropping the member to the free tier.

In the Members list, a member who pays through Stripe now shows what they pay for next to a box for the gift, so you can see at a glance what they are billed and what they can use.

Updating from inside the app actually works now - and if it ever fails, it says so. This was the big one. Pressing "Check for updates" downloaded the new version, closed Jolnova, and then nothing happened: the app came back on the old version with no explanation. Measured on a real machine, the installer log said why - the file could not be replaced because a second copy of Jolnova was still running, and the silent installer answers that question with "abort". The update script only waited for the copy that started it. It now closes every running copy first, gently and then firmly, before installing. It also writes down what happened, so the next time Jolnova opens it either says "Update complete" and lets you carry on, or tells you exactly what went wrong and where to download it by hand. Previously a failure was written to a console window nobody could see - and that line was itself broken, so it never even paused.

A new version now announces itself. There was only a thin strip at the top of the window, which is easy to miss when the app is left open for days - which is how it is meant to be used. Jolnova now opens a proper dialog once, after it has finished starting, with the headline change and an Update now button. The strip is still there.

A plan cannot be changed by hand for someone who pays through Stripe - and this was silently breaking things. Three separate problems, all measured in the code. It did not last: the payment provider writes the plan back at the next renewal, so a plan set by hand quietly disappeared a month later and the member lost the features. It broke the revenue figure: setting a plan by hand marks the row as granted, and that is what decides whether a subscription counts as revenue - answering "gift" made a member who really pays vanish from the monthly total, while answering "payment received" logged the new plan's price instead of what they actually pay. And it never changed the money: nothing here talks to the payment provider, so the card went on being charged the old price. Those members now show a locked plan with the reason, and the server refuses the change even if the screen is out of date. To really move someone to another plan, change their subscription in Stripe - the difference is charged there and the new plan arrives here by itself.

Paying customers could be shown "Your free trial has ended". This is the one that mattered. The screen that checks your account gave up after a couple of tries, and on a slow connection - or when the sign-in token had just expired - those tries ran out before the answer arrived, so a subscriber who had paid real money was told their trial was over. It now refreshes the token and keeps asking for about sixteen seconds before it concludes anything, and it re-checks by itself the moment you sign in. Nobody who has paid should see that message again.

The user guide is visible to everyone. It was accidentally placed inside the admin-only part of the menu, so ordinary users - the people it was written for - could not see it at all. It now sits in the main menu under Clip Style, for every account.

Subscribe opens the pricing page. Pressing it used to jump straight into the card form for one particular plan, with no way to see what the plans are or compare them. It now opens jolnova.com/pricing, where you choose first. After you come back, Jolnova keeps checking your account for ten minutes and tells you as soon as the subscription is active - you no longer have to restart it or press anything.

Jolnova opens maximised. It asked the window manager for a maximised window and then accepted whatever it got, which on some machines was a small window in the corner. It now maximises the window itself once it appears.

Assigning a plan by hand works without the admin key. It needed a secret server key that is not in the app, so the button existed but always failed. It now writes with your own admin sign-in.

Assigning a plan by hand no longer disturbs a real subscription. If you set a plan for someone who pays through Stripe, their billing period used to be overwritten with a fresh year, so our records said they were paid up until next September while Stripe went on charging monthly. The dates Stripe writes are now left alone. Note that Stripe remains in charge of what is charged: a plan you set by hand for a paying customer is a gift on top of what they pay, and it reverts at their next renewal - to really change what someone pays, change their subscription in Stripe.

The Automatic / Game / IRL buttons are gone from the add-source row. They did nothing there: Jolnova asks you the same question in the window that opens when you add a source.
